subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should persisted `/exec` session defaults continue to override later agent/global exec policy, or should operator-controlled config/security policy take precedence after config changes and resets?
rationale: Current docs and tests encode durable per-session defaults, but the reported behavior affects the operator exec security boundary, so automation should not pick a new precedence contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Make operator policy dominate
options.body: Treat persisted `/exec` fields as resettable or lower-priority state when operator exec policy changes, and add focused migration/reset coverage for existing sessions.

options.title: Keep durable session defaults
options.body: Preserve current `/exec` semantics and document/admin-surface the expected reset path for operators who need to clear stored exec policy.

options.title: Add explicit reset tooling first
options.body: Keep current precedence but add doctor or session-reset behavior that safely clears stored exec fields before considering a precedence change.

recommendation.title: Make operator policy dominate
recommendation.body: Treat persisted `/exec` fields as resettable or lower-priority state when operator exec policy changes, and add focused migration/reset coverage for existing sessions.

likelyOwner.reason: The original `/exec` session override behavior, docs, and focused resolver coverage trace most directly to steipete-authored commits.
